title: PowerPoint on desktop: reference a PowerPoint file when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: the briefing treats the licence tier for an editing workflow as unpublished, but Microsoft's service description identifies edit with Copilot in PowerPoint as a Premium capability requiring a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. It also claims the listed controls cover the source-deck exposure without evidence that they govern explicitly referenced files.

claims.claim: Licences can be assigned through Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote:
go to the Users > Active users page.
Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to.
In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps.
Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses

claims.claim: The printed Set-MgUserLicense call assigns a licence to the specified user using the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: At least License Administrator or User Administrator is required to assign licences.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level control limiting SharePoint content discovery in organisation-wide search and Microsoft Copilot responses.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect experiences operating on content already in use by the user.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.
